title: Reading a damped oscillation
summary: Use a normalized waveform to read the period of a ringing signal and the rate at which its amplitude decays.
brief: A ringing trace contains two useful time scales. The spacing between successive peaks gives the oscillation period. The change in peak height tells us how quickly the oscillation dies away.
design: The welcome-page illustration plots a sine wave multiplied by a decaying exponential, after a short delay. The horizontal and vertical scales are normalized. This is a mathematical illustration, so the trace carries no physical time or voltage units.
results: Successive positive peaks get closer to the baseline even as their spacing stays constant. On a measured trace, recording both peak spacing and peak height would let us describe frequency and damping separately.
alt: Green oscillation on a scope grid with constant peak spacing and decreasing amplitude.
